review.tagline: Python toolkit for loading, annotating and counting computer vision detections
review.summary: Supervision is a model-agnostic Python library that wraps detection, classification and segmentation outputs in a common sv.Detections object. It has connectors for Ultralytics, Transformers, MMDetection and Inference, annotators for drawing results, and utilities to load, split, merge and convert YOLO, Pascal VOC and COCO datasets. Tracking, zone counting and speed estimation appear in the linked tutorials.
review.audience: Python developers building computer vision apps around detection models
strengths: Connectors for Ultralytics, Transformers, MMDetection and Inference; rfdetr returns sv.Detections directly
Dataset utils load, split, merge and convert YOLO, Pascal VOC and COCO
Configurable annotators such as BoxAnnotator for drawing detections on frames
Installs with pip; docs, cookbooks and a cheatsheet are available
weaknesses: Does not train or run models itself; a separate detection model is required
Inference and dataset download examples need a Roboflow API key
Tracking and zone features are shown in video tutorials, not the README text
needs: Needs Python>=3.10, rfdetr (optional), Roboflow Inference (optional), Roboflow API key (optional)
Models: Ultralytics, Transformers, MMDetection, Inference, rfdetr
